version: v13.4 hub (SKILL.md line 6: "readymerce-ads-machine (v13.4 hub: ..."; changelog line 1978 dated 2026-10-11). Section G content is the v13.3 rewrite (2026-10-08, line 1979).
purpose: This is the hub skill for cold, paid Meta ads in any niche. It covers Module 0 (brief, VOC research, desire stack, belief ledger, concept memo, budget sizing, Voice Card B1, Conviction Map B2), Part L copy laws, Part A statics, Part B long-form native story ads (28 swipes), and Part C video core (the C3 build order, the hook card in C5, the length tiers in C6, formats, treatments, C12 tests, the C13 Meta test plan, C17 transpositions). It also holds Section G, the production hard gates for every AI video: MiniMax H3 at 2K, Kling fallback, budget preflight, one speaker per generation, no filler, transcript and drift check, GPT Image 2 stills, and every voice, music bed and SFX from ElevenLabs. Podcast, animation and drama production is routed to role skills. Hooks go to readymerce-hook-lab and scripts to readymerce-script-lab. references/production.md is a statics-only ledger, prompt handoff and delivery layout. Everything is built around paid Meta ads: a Shop Now CTA, offer and guarantee, and ad-set metrics.

phases.name: Read Appendix M (Copy Laws reference)
phases.does: Loads readymerce-script-lab and reads its Appendix M in full before any copy is written.
phases.gate: Once per session: "if it has not been read in this session" (line 1631). Mandatory before any copy (line 27).

phases.name: Brief intake
phases.does: Collects 13 required items: product truth, avatars (with age band and platform), VOC bank, desire map, belief ledger, UMP/UMS mechanism, awareness scope, current offer, destination with its mechanism-match words, budget/CPA/AOV, count/market/aspect, the outcome the brand stands behind (feeds the Result Ladder), and the factory questions.
phases.gate: Hard stop without VOC: "This skill cannot run without VOC. If none exists, stop and ask for it, or run a VOC harvest first." (line 491). "Do not silently pick an avatar, awareness level or offer." (line 506)
phases.human_checkpoint: Ask for all missing items "together in one concise intake" (line 506). Stop and ask if VOC is missing (lines 491, 977). Result Ladder rung 3: "ask the brand once" (line 1332). No numbered GATE.

phases.name: Commercial pre-flight
phases.does: Flags offer vs CPA, price match, page congruency, tracking and offer strength at the top of the concept slate.
phases.gate: Report only, never blocks: "Do not block the batch." (line 510). This is a paid/DTC check that does not apply to organic posts.

phases.name: Research: benefit ladder, language harvest, desire stack, belief ledger, white space
phases.does: Ranks verbatim phrases by charge (1 to 5) with slot, OWNED-VOC/MKT-LANG/WRITTEN tag, extraction tag and source tier. Picks 1 to 2 LF8 roots per avatar, builds 5+ angles per desire, records 3 to 6 beliefs per avatar, and runs a competitor white-space scan that also logs the sophistication stage.
phases.gate: The harvest holds "at least 3 accommodations, 3 failed solutions and, when owned sources exist, 1 nearly-didn't per avatar" (line 541). "Do not open the image tool until A2 to A4 are done." (line 520)
phases.tools_models: Web/VOC research. Use AI only to retrieve real quotes (line 164)

phases.name: Concept memo
phases.does: Writes WHAT, WHY, HOW, STAMP (awareness plus sophistication), DESIRE EVIDENCE and LOAD-BEARING BEAT. A concept is avatar + desire (LF8) + angle + target belief + offer.
phases.gate: "A concept whose WHY rests on no quotes is cut." (line 602). One avatar per concept. Launch wave is 100% net-new.
phases.human_checkpoint: Concept slate shown to the user (implicit). No numbered GATE.

phases.name: Size the batch to the budget
phases.does: Sets concepts, ads per concept and max live cold ads from the daily budget table. About 1 new ad per $1,000 of monthly spend.
phases.gate: Concepts launched is about daily budget ÷ target CPA, capped by the table. Extras are marked benched. Paid only.

phases.name: Structure model
phases.does: Picks one B19 swipe by angle type and notes the devices to borrow: carrier, analogy, physical demo, money math, second sufferer, log, callback.
phases.gate: Silent unless the user asks
phases.tools_models: B19 library (references/msl-swipe-file.pdf is referenced but missing)

phases.name: Voice Card (B1)
phases.does: Builds a one-page card per avatar with 11 items: their words, scenes, internal dialogue, failed-solution list, tired-of-hearing, self-blame, fears, desire, doubts, rhythm, accommodations.
phases.gate: "Pull 10 or more verbatim phrases ... including at least one accommodation" (line 1634). Every struggle or emotional beat carries a trace tag `← Q-##`; a beat with no trace is rewritten or cut (lines 997-998).

phases.name: Conviction Map (B2)
phases.does: Maps 9 beliefs (this is me ... now) to the scene that installs each one. Script Lab turns it into the belief ladder.
phases.gate: "Each belief lands inside a scene, never as a lecture." (line 1017)

phases.name: Brief card (Script Lab 2a)
phases.does: Assembles avatar, starting belief, target belief, desire, stamp, angle, accommodations/moments/failed fixes, mechanism and its picture, product truth, offer and proof facts with sources.
phases.gate: "A missing fact is found in the project, or the line that needs it is cut; it is never invented." (line 1636)

phases.name: Job, tiers, format, treatment
phases.does: Names the load-bearing beat, scores formats on six properties, chooses STORY/CONVERSATION/DEMO and the router tiers (D15 to V300), and writes the awareness stamp on the script.
phases.gate: "Every concept gets a short tier and a story tier (C6); L150 and V300 need a stated reason." (line 1637). "No story under 55 s." (line 1651)

phases.name: Hook Lab (C5 hook card)
phases.does: Checks Hook Library freshness, then generates and grades hook stacks (visual + text + spoken). Keeps 3 stacks (a master and 2 variants, at least 2 hook types), each with a concept frame.
phases.gate: Hook Library "under 60 days old" (line 1638). All 9 gates pass and every channel scores A or A+; an A- is rewritten (line 1688). Text is 4 to 10 words; spoken sentence 1 is 8 to 14 words with the first word at 0.0 s. "No script line is written before this." (line 1638)
phases.human_checkpoint: Stacks are "picked at the script gate" (line 1693). No numbered GATE.
phases.tools_models: Skill readymerce-hook-lab. Concept frames come from an image model (not named in the hub)

phases.name: Script Lab WRITE
phases.does: Writes the persona card and the pre-write pack (belief ladder with the because test, question chain, script bible, reveal plan). Writes 2 or 3 spines of about 80 words and picks one. Each tier is then written from the spine on its own, with a line table.
phases.gate: Inside its word budget at "2.5 words a second before casting" (line 1639). Core lines under 12 words, none over 17, grade 7 (line 1653). Never trimmed from a longer cut.

phases.name: Script Lab gate and release + C11 script table
phases.does: Runs 16 tests plus the lessons list, a cold read by a fresh agent (plus a skeptical second reader from S90 up) and a 100-point score. Then writes the C11 script table.
phases.gate: "release at 85 or more with no critical fail, up to 3 FIX loops" (line 1640). Test 12 seam-checks the 3 hook stacks; a failing stack goes back to Hook Lab H6.
phases.human_checkpoint: "Up to 3 rewrite loops, then the user decides." (line 1654)
phases.tools_models: readymerce-script-lab plus a fresh subagent for the cold read

phases.name: Visual plan
phases.does: Frame 1 is the master stack's approved hook frame. A picture for every claim, an Invisible-Made-Visible shot for the mechanism, and character and product references.
phases.gate: Feeds the C12 tests

phases.name: Video-level tests (C12) + read-aloud
phases.does: Runs the non-Script-Lab C12 tests (2, 3, 4, 12, 14, 16 to 20, 22, 23, 25, 26, 28, 29, 29b, 30, 31, 35, 40) on the script table and visual plan, then reads the script out loud at real speed.
phases.gate: "Any fail means a rewrite before anything is filmed or generated" (line 1642). Test 29: H3 clips 5 to 15 s. Test 29b: every generation passes Section G.

phases.name: Budget preflight
phases.does: Prices one clip with a cost check, multiplies by all clips and seconds, adds a retake allowance, and checks the balance.
phases.gate: Check the balance "right before submitting, not only at the start" (line 99). "Never start an ad you can't finish."
phases.human_checkpoint: "If the balance can't cover the whole ad, say so and agree the scope before spending anything." (line 99)

phases.name: Stills (characters, sets, cutaway stills)
phases.does: Makes realistic people from a reference image, written as an iPhone candid with a moving background and empty hands, plus one extra still per setting for cutaways. Locks them as references.
phases.gate: GPT Image 2 (`gpt_image_2`, quality high, 2k), "never from text alone" (line 109). Never cinematic, studio or bokeh (line 110). Stylized work keeps the style skill's model (line 114).
phases.human_checkpoint: The "person's approved still for identity" implies approval (line 109). No numbered GATE.

phases.name: Voice, music, SFX
phases.does: Casts a library or designed voice and generates beats of 2 to 7 lines at 4 takes each, checking every take against the script. Makes music beds (2 takes) and SFX.
phases.gate: eleven_v4 is the default, with eleven_v3 auditioned. Never compress or cap human pauses. Each take needs pause SD of 0.1 s or more and a few pauses of 0.45 s or more at sentence ends (line 120). Negations must survive the transcript (line 121).
phases.human_checkpoint: none in the hub (animation Phase 5 has the user pick by ear)
phases.tools_models: ElevenLabs creative_generate_speech (eleven_v4/eleven_v3), eleven_music_v2_5, eleven_text_to_sound_v2, voice-changer eleven_multilingual_sts_v2. vo_build2.py (lives in animation Phase 5)

phases.name: Per-speaker stems and slices
phases.does: Packs each speaker's consecutive lines into slices of up to 15 s from their own stem. One speaker per generation; a setting change starts a new clip.
phases.gate: About 30 to 35 words per 15 s clip. Never split a line (rewrite lines over about 35 words). Slice padded to whole seconds, minimum 5 s (lines 81, 83, 101).

phases.name: Video generation
phases.does: Runs H3 reference mode (stills + voice slice) for talking shots and keyframe mode for shots with no mouth on the voice. Every prompt follows the 7-part H3 prompt card. Kling 3.0 is used only for a non-talking transformation after the H3 keyframe take fails.
phases.gate: minimax_h3, 2K, 9:16, 5 to 15 s, declined_preset_id on every call. 2 to 4 shots per clip, one action per shot, a background line in every shot, at most one gesture per shot. No filler or listening clips (G5). The hook storyboard is checked at phone size first and the hook sequence is rendered twice (line 1693).
phases.human_checkpoint: Overriding a hard gate needs a single confirmation (line 78)

phases.name: Transcript and drift check
phases.does: Transcribes every speaking clip with Whisper word timestamps and diffs it against the script. Drift-checks every H3 talking clip, fixes drift in the edit with jump cuts at pauses or a median offset, and mutes clip audio so the ElevenLabs master is the timeline.
phases.gate: Retake only for a missing, wrong or added word the edit can't cut around, or drift inside a word (lines 105-106). No numeric retake cap.

phases.name: Edit
phases.does: Bold sans captions at 2 to 4 words per line inside the safe zone. Cuts on the speech beat, SFX on reveals, music low and ducked under the hook, aha and payoff. Review cards run 2 to 3 s. End card is the last 2 s with the 3-word outcome and the offer line. Text is added in the edit only.
phases.gate: Safe zone: top 14% and bottom 20% clear (line 1622). No em dashes in spoken lines, supers or captions (line 1803).

phases.name: More lengths (Script Lab LADDER)
phases.does: Writes each extra tier from the spine with its own bridges, hook and gate.
phases.gate: Never trimmed from the master. Each tier has its own release.

phases.name: Deliver
phases.does: Delivers the script file (C11 template), short tiers, shot list and prompt sheet, 3 hook stacks as cut instructions, primary text/headline/CTA, test plan, diversity table, Script Lab release and C12 results, saved with the batch.
phases.gate: production.md delivery layout (statics-oriented). No video ledger is defined.
phases.human_checkpoint: Publishing needs separate user authorization (production.md line 89)

phases.name: Test plan and LEARN
phases.does: Runs videos in the concept ad set and reads hook rate, hold rate, link CTR, ATC and purchase after about 1,000 impressions. Maps drop-offs to lines with Script Lab LEARN. Iteration order: new hook stacks, new short tier, transposition (C17), new body, new format.
phases.gate: Hook rate floor 30% (re-hook under 25%), target 40%, stretch 50%. Hold floor 25%, target 35%. Link CTR above about 1%. Decisions at ad-set level (A19/B17).

numbers.value: MiniMax H3 (minimax_h3) for every video generation in every module
numbers.quote: **G1. Every AI video: MiniMax H3 at 2K.** Every video generation in every module runs on MiniMax H3 (`minimax_h3`), `resolution: "2K"`, `aspect_ratio: "9:16"` (unless the placement needs another ratio)

numbers.value: 2K
numbers.quote: `resolution: "2K"`

numbers.value: 9:16 unless the placement needs another; master framed 4:5-safe
numbers.quote: Default master: 9:16 with 4:5-safe framing

numbers.value: Talking shots: stills as image_references (up to 9, storyboard/start still first) + ElevenLabs slice as audio_references
numbers.quote: **Reference mode for every shot where a mouth moves:** `medias` = the character or scene still(s) as `image_references` (up to 9; the storyboard or start still first) plus the ElevenLabs voice slice as `audio_references`.

numbers.value: Start frame + optional end frame, no refs, no audio; modes never mixed
numbers.quote: **Keyframe mode for shots with no mouth on the voice:** a start frame and an optional end frame, no references, no audio. The two modes cannot be mixed in one generation.

numbers.value: duration = padded slice length (slice padded with silence to whole seconds)
numbers.quote: The slice starts on the clip's first frame and is padded with silence to a whole number of seconds; `duration` = that padded length.

numbers.value: 5 to 15 s (4 s failed)
numbers.quote: **Clip length 5 to 15 seconds.** 15 seconds is the H3 maximum; a 4-second render failed in testing, so pad any shorter slice to 5 seconds.

numbers.value: 3 to 8 s per b-roll/action shot (conflicts with the 5 s minimum)
numbers.quote: **One shot = one clip of 3 to 8 seconds with one action** (b-roll and action shots; talking clips follow G4).

numbers.value: C12 test 29: H3 5 to 15 s
numbers.quote: 29. **Producible:** every shot can be filmed or generated within its model's clip limits (H3: 5 to 15 seconds; talking characters: one speaker per generation, lines packed per G4).

numbers.value: 24bae836-2c4a-48e0-89b6-49fcc0b21612 on every H3 and Kling call
numbers.quote: **Pass `declined_preset_id: "24bae836-2c4a-48e0-89b6-49fcc0b21612"`** on every H3 (and Kling) call, or the API recommends a preset instead of submitting the job.

numbers.value: Never FLUX 3, Seedance, Veo, Sora, Grok, Gemini/Omni, Wan, Hailuo unless the user names the model
numbers.quote: Never FLUX 3, Seedance, Veo, Sora, Grok, Gemini/Omni, Wan or Hailuo, for any clip, take, test or fix, unless the user names the model.

numbers.value: Kling 3.0 only for a non-talking transformation after an H3 keyframe take fails, or on request; Seedance never
numbers.quote: Use Kling 3.0 (`kling3_0`, start and end frame) only for a non-talking start-to-end transformation (a box filling up, a bubble changing colour) after an H3 keyframe take of it fails the frame check, or when the user asks for it. Seedance is never used.

numbers.value: about 30 to 35 words (2 or 3 short lines) per 15 s clip; lines over about 35 words split into two turns
numbers.quote: With H3 that means about 30 to 35 words (2 or 3 short lines) per 15-second clip, cut from that speaker's own voice stem; when a speaker has more, pack consecutive lines up to 15 seconds and start their next clip. Never split a line across clips (rewrite a line over about 35 words into two turns)

numbers.value: 2 to 4 shots per clip, one action per shot
numbers.quote: **Timeline:** "Shot N, a to b s:" with ONE action per shot, timed to the words ("on the words '...' he ..."), 2 to 4 shots per clip, joined by named cuts.

numbers.value: 2 or 3 named people doing a named action in every shot
numbers.quote: **Background line in every shot:** 2 or 3 named people doing a named action (walks across with a coffee, laughs on a call, stands up and stretches). Without it H3 freezes everyone but the speaker.

numbers.value: at most one gesture per shot
numbers.quote: Keep gestures small and few (one per shot at most): every gesture written into the prompt gets acted out, and big ones read as pantomime.

numbers.value: every 1.5 to 3 s (UGC/b-roll); talking head holds 4 to 6 s
numbers.quote: A new shot or visual change every 1.5 to 3 seconds in UGC and b-roll formats; a strong talking head can hold 4 to 6 seconds; the payoff can hold longer.

numbers.value: GPT Image 2 (gpt_image_2), quality high, 2k, always with a reference image
numbers.quote: **Realistic people: GPT Image 2 (`gpt_image_2`, quality high, 2k) with a reference image** (a real candid photo from the casting search, or the person's approved still for identity), never from text alone.

numbers.value: GPT Image 2.5 rejected for faces (plastic skin)
numbers.quote: GPT Image 2.5 smoothed the skin into a plastic look on the round 5 UGC people (Oct 2026); GPT Image 2 with a reference kept pores and fine lines.

numbers.value: style skill's own model
numbers.quote: Stylized work keeps the style skill's model.

numbers.value: iPhone 15 Pro candid; never cinematic, studio, bokeh or film grain
numbers.quote: Never cinematic, studio, bokeh, film grain or a camera brand other than the phone.

numbers.value: one extra still per setting, made with the main still as reference
numbers.quote: **One extra still per setting for cutaways** (the room from another angle, the team, the product), made with the main still as the reference so the place matches.

numbers.value: concurrency 8 or fewer, high quality for finals
numbers.quote: Concurrency 8 or fewer, high quality for finals.

numbers.value: ElevenLabs eleven_v4 default, eleven_v3 auditioned
numbers.quote: `creative_generate_speech`, model `eleven_v4` by default (audition `eleven_v3` beside it)

numbers.quote: `eleven_v3` ran Albanian lines together with almost no pauses in the same test; `eleven_v4` stays the default.

numbers.value: 2.5 words/s before casting (15s about 35, 30s about 70, 60s about 150, 90s about 220, 120s about 300 words); measured pace after casting
numbers.quote: Speaking rate before casting is about 2.5 words per second: 15s is about 35 words, 30s about 70, 60s about 150, 90s about 220, 120s about 300. After casting, count at the voice's measured pace.

numbers.value: never compress or cap; pause SD of 0.1 s or more; a few pauses of 0.45 s or more at sentence ends; natural take had 0.2 to 0.6 s
numbers.quote: Check every take before use: pause count, spread (standard deviation 0.1 seconds or more) and a few pauses of 0.45 seconds or more at sentence ends.

numbers.value: no pause capping on human voices (0.30 s cap made the voice robotic)
numbers.quote: **Natural pauses, never tightened.** Never compress or cap the pauses of a human voice (UGC, podcast, talking head).

numbers.value: No speed-up number. A long take is fixed by cutting words or moving up a tier
numbers.quote: Keep the model's own pauses; if a take runs long, cut words in the script (Script Lab) or move up a tier.

numbers.value: eleven_multilingual_sts_v2; onsets within 0.02 s; about 17 credits/s per take
numbers.quote: Tested Oct 2026: same words, word onsets within 0.02 seconds on average, so the lips stay in sync; about 17 credits a second per take.

numbers.quote: **Music beds:** `eleven_music_v2_5`, instrumental, 2 takes. **Sound effects:** `eleven_text_to_sound_v2`. A licensed track the user supplies is fine. Song ads keep Suno for the song itself (`readymerce-song-ads`).

visual_qa_overlap:
The hub already covers several QA points. (1) H3 prompt card (G1, lines 86-95): a 7-part prompt order (realism line, reference tokens in upload order, hands and props, shot timeline with 2 to 4 shots and named cuts, background action in every shot, lip-sync block with pause times, negatives), at most one small gesture per shot, and known H3 failures (frozen background, vanishing phone, a skipped cut, last-line drift). (2) G7 still rules: GPT Image 2 with a reference image, iPhone-candid wording, people in the background mid-action, empty hands, no stray props, one extra still per setting for cutaways. (3) G6: Whisper word-timestamp transcript diff on every speaking clip, plus an audio-envelope drift check (2 s windows every 0.25 s) with edit-side fixes and retake conditions. (4) G8 take checks: pause count, SD of 0.1 s or more, pauses of 0.45 s or more, negations confirmed in the transcript. (5) C5 hook card: concept frame per stack, hook storyboard checked at phone size with the text on it, hook sequence rendered twice. (6) C10b negative prompt list and product-reference rules, plus C10c \"QA every frame\" for stylized frames (character match, label, one of each object, no stray text, ratio; reroll failures). (7) A22 and references/production.md static inspection: full size and phone size, contact sheets, closest-pair audit, measured pixel dimensions, qa.status pending/pass, and audit_batch.py, which is structural only and does no image decoding. (8) The only fresh-agent review in the system is Script Lab's cold read of the script (persona card + script only, skeptical second reader from S90 up).

All visual QA is self-check by the same agent that generated the work. C0's \"the writer grades his own script\" failure was fixed for scripts but not for visuals. The hub gives no frame-sampling rate for clips, no storyboard layout spec (that lives in the animation and song skills), no take-review rubric, no numeric retake cap, no final-file check (loudness, fps, resolution, safe-zone overlay, caption/transcript match), and no video/clip ledger (production.md is statics-only).

A fresh-agent reviewer stack would replace or add the following. (a) A Prompt Reviewer before every submit that lints each H3 prompt against the 7-part card: every token maps to an uploaded media in order, every prop in the still has a hand instruction, 2 to 4 shots with one action each, a background line in every shot, pause times copied from the slice, negatives present, duration = slice rules, declined_preset_id and the model/2K/9:16 params. It acts as a blocking G-SPEC gate and replaces the G1 self-check. (b) A Visual Reviewer for stills and storyboards before lock, checking the G7 rules (pores and no plastic skin, background mid-action, empty hands, no extra objects, identity match to the reference, cutaway still matches the place, readable at phone size, hook text area clear), replacing C10c and A22 self-inspection. (c) A Take Reviewer on each generated clip that samples frames (e.g. every 0.5 s plus a contact sheet), reads the Whisper diff and drift numbers, and scores identity drift, prop continuity, frozen background, skipped cuts, mouth closed in pauses, morphing, text artifacts and end-of-clip drift. It returns keep / fix-in-edit / retake with a retake cap, replacing the generator's own G6 judgement. (d) A Final-cut Reviewer that watches at phone size with an IG UI overlay and checks the safe zone, captions against the transcript, loudness and true peak, fps and resolution, the AI label set, the CTA keyword matching the DM funnel, and the 3-second sound-off hook test (C12 tests 18 and 20).
